utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: As said --

utterances.speaker: SIMO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- going directly from the command to the soldiers in the brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: As assistant commander for morale, religious, and legal affairs, to whom were you subordinate, Mr. Zaric?

utterances.speaker: SIMO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was directly subordinated to the commander of the 2nd Posavina Brigade, Commander Beronja, according to the chain of command. And according to the chain of subordination, my superior at that time was Zivko Dosen who was the assistant commander of the East Bosnia Corps. He was a colonel and he was also in charge of morale, religious, and legal affairs.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Zaric, to whom did you report on your work or the work of the organ you were in charge of?

utterances.speaker: SIMO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had to give detailed reports according to a certain procedure to the assistant commander of the East Bosnia Corps for morale, religious, and legal matters, but the reports I sent and the documents could never be dispatched unless they were signed, not just by me but also by the commander of the 2nd Posavina Infantry Brigade. This was the regular procedure that had to be implemented according to the regulations that were then in force.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Zaric, as assistant commander for morale, religious, and legal affairs, who gave you your orders and the instructions for the work of this organ?

utterances.speaker: SIMO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was again in two ways: From the assistant commander of the East Bosnia Corps for morale and religious affairs, while part of my tasks directly stemmed from what came from the commander or the command, if the command adopted certain conclusions, and in the nature of the work, they were directly connected with what I and my men were to do, because I didn't work alone. I had a team of men working in my organ.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you, at the same time, have the status of a member of the command of the 2nd Posavina Infantry Brigade of the army of Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: SIMO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I had the status of a member of the command, and according to importance, I was the third most responsible man, according to the hierarchy in the command of the 2nd Posavina Brigade. At the top was the commander, then there was the Chief of Staff, and the third man would be the assistant for morale, and then I won't enumerate anymore.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: No. No, don't. But if you can remember, please tell us: How many members did the command of the 2nd Posavina Brigade have?

utterances.speaker: SIMO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think the command had about 15 members, including the headquarters command, and those in charge of civilian affairs. But when we started, it had 13 members, at the time I was transferred there.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Zaric, you have already said that the commander of the 2nd Posavina Infantry Brigade was Major Mile Beronja. You have not told us, however, so far, who was the commander of the East Bosnia Corps of the army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: SIMO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time, when I was transferred to the duty of assistant commander, the duty of commander of the East Bosnia Corps was performed by Colonel Novica Simic, and that was the colonel who was the first commander of the military administration in Odzak, who stayed there for a very brief period of time. And after him, a new colonel was appointed. I can't remember his name, but I know that they were changed very quickly. But Novica Simic was a colonel, was the commander of the East Bosnia Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: You have described the situation in the brigade that you found as regards morale, religious, and legal affairs. Tell us, please: What did you do when you first arrived in order to make sure that this body fulfilled its tasks?

utterances.speaker: SIMO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In view of the level of responsibility that was given to me, I first studied the rules and regulations governing the work of the assistant commander for morale, religious, and legal affairs. And then I studied the methodology and the procedures as to how reports should be drawn up on the morale situation and all other relevant issues, and submitted to my command, and that was the command of the East Bosnia Corps, and within that, the 2nd Posavina Infantry Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: I will now put a few questions to you to try and clarify the chain of command in the army. The lower-level units, such as battalions, for example, did they also have their organ for morale, religious, and legal affairs, and did they have their assistant commanders for these tasks?

utterances.speaker: SIMO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Every infantry battalion, and later on there were seven infantry battalions and not only five in the brigade, after the reorganisation. And there were independent units, engineering units, artillery units, and so on. Each of these units and each infantry battalion, under the rulings and regulations, had a post in its command of assistant commander for morale, religious, and legal affairs.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: And you, as the assistants commander for morale, religious, and legal affairs, what was your relationship with the assistant commanders for these same matters in the battalions and independent companies and so on?

utterances.speaker: SIMO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To put it very simply, what the assistant commander for religious and legal affairs and morale was for me at the level of the East Bosnia Corps, on a smaller scale, I represented the same thing for all these other assistant commanders in all the other units of the 2nd Posavina Infantry Brigade. I cooperated with them, and it was their duty to submit reports to me as to the situation regarding morale, religious, and legal affairs in their units.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Zaric, when you took up the post of assistant commander for morale, religious, and legal affairs, did you draw up a report on the situation that you had found as to morale in the 2nd Posavina Infantry Brigade?

utterances.speaker: SIMO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Every month, reports had to be written and submitted to the Superior Command. On my arrival, some 10 or 15 days later, I actively toured all the units, desiring to take stock of the situation, as fully as possible, in order to draw up a full report and submit this to my command, the 2nd Posavina Infantry Brigade, and also, of course, to the command of the East Bosnia Corps, and this is what I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: This first report of yours which you drew up, was it considered in the command of the 2nd Posavina Infantry Brigade in Pelagicevo?

utterances.speaker: SIMO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Every one of my reports was considered, and so was this one.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: And when the command acquainted itself with your first report as to the morale situation in the brigade and the morale of the organs for morale, religious, and legal affairs, what did the command decide? What did it decide should be done, in view of the situation that you discovered on your arrival, in order to improve the situation?

utterances.speaker: SIMO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In view of the fact that I was perhaps slightly too critical in my description of the situation, I was told to review the situation in detail in each unit and draw attention to all those elements that were leading to a decline in morale among the soldiers, and as reflected in the rear, on the population living in the area of responsibility of the 2nd Posavina Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I think it is time to conclude for the day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. We shall adjourn and continue our proceedings tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 13th day of May 2003, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 4.15 p.m.,
